answer:
For an **additional ETF series in an existing registered trust**, a Rule **485(a)(2)** post-effective amendment normally becomes effective **75 calendar days after filing**—not the 60-day period generally applicable to other Rule 485(a) amendments. Acceleration or a later effective date can change that timing.

That is a **registration-effectiveness timetable, not an end-to-end launch guarantee**. SEC comments and necessary revisions, exchange listing approval, operational readiness, seed capital, and service-provider/authorized-participant arrangements may affect when trading starts. Not needing separate exemptive relief removes one potential hurdle, not all launch requirements.

**A new trust is different:** its initial registration statement is not a Rule 485 post-effective amendment. It ordinarily undergoes SEC review and becomes effective through an SEC declaration, with delaying amendments typically preventing automatic effectiveness; the 75-day new-series rule does not apply.
